title: Handicrafts of India: Crafts, Artisan Villages and Where to Buy
seoTitle: Handicrafts of India: Crafts by Region | Kudozz Club
metaDescription: India's handicrafts by region, and where to see them made: blue pottery, block printing, Bidriware, dhokra, Pattachitra, Madhubani, Channapatna toys and more.
description: A traveller's guide to the handicrafts of India, region by region: Jaipur blue pottery and Sanganer block printing, Kutch embroidery and bandhani, Kashmiri papier-mache, Bidriware, Channapatna toys, dhokra metal casting, Pattachitra at Raghurajpur, Madhubani painting, Bankura terracotta and more, with craft villages to visit, fairs, and how to buy ethically.
dek: Indian crafts are made by families and communities who have passed their skills down for generations. Seeing them at work is one of the best parts of a heritage trip.

hero.alt: Shelves of Jaipur blue pottery in a craft shop

intro: India has an extraordinary range of crafts: pottery, metalwork, painting, woodwork, stone carving, embroidery and more, often tied to a single town or community. Many have a Geographical Indication (GI) tag, which protects the name for products made in that place.

The best way to understand a craft is to see it being made, in a craft village, a workshop or a fair, and to buy directly from the people who make it. This guide covers crafts by region; textiles have their own guide.
quickAnswer: India's best-known handicrafts include Jaipur blue pottery, block printing at Sanganer and Bagru, Kutch embroidery, Bidriware from Bidar, Channapatna wooden toys, dhokra metal casting from Bastar and Bengal, Pattachitra painting at Raghurajpur in Odisha, Madhubani painting from Bihar, Kashmiri papier-mache, and Bankura's terracotta horses. Craft villages and fairs such as Surajkund are the best places to see them made.
takeaways: Many crafts are tied to one town and protected by GI tags.
Raghurajpur (Odisha) and the villages around Bhuj (Kutch) are among the best craft villages to visit.
Craft fairs such as Surajkund near Delhi bring artisans from across India.
Buying directly from artisans or cooperatives supports them most.
Textiles, such as silk and handloom saris, are covered in our textile guide.

items.name: Jaipur and around
body: Blue pottery workshops, block printers at Sanganer and Bagru, and gem cutting and enamelling in the walled city.

items.name: Kutch
body: Villages around Bhuj are known for embroidery, bandhani (tie-dye), Ajrakh printing, rogan painting and bell making.

items.name: Raghurajpur, Odisha
body: A village near Puri where almost every house paints Pattachitra and palm-leaf engravings. It is also known for the Gotipua dance tradition.

items.name: Madhubani, Bihar
body: Mithila painting, traditionally done by women on walls and floors for festivals and weddings.

items.name: Bengal
body: Bankura's terracotta horses, dhokra casting and Bishnupur's crafts, and Kolkata's Kumartuli idol-makers.

items.name: Karnataka and Tamil Nadu
body: Channapatna toys on the Bengaluru to Mysuru road, Bidriware in Bidar, stone carving in Mahabalipuram, bronze casting at Swamimalai near Kumbakonam.

sections.heading: Buying ethically
list: Buy from government emporia, cooperatives, certified sellers or artisans directly; look for GI tags, Silk Mark or Handloom Mark where they apply, and be wary of 'factory visits' arranged by touts.
Ask who made a piece and where; good sellers will tell you.
Hand-made pieces vary slightly; perfect uniformity often means machine production.
Bargain politely in markets, but not with artisans at fair-price cooperatives.

sections.heading: Kashmir and Uttar Pradesh
paras: Srinagar's old city is known for papier-mache, walnut-wood carving, hand-knotted carpets and crewel embroidery, and you can visit workshops in the lanes around the Jhelum. In Uttar Pradesh, Moradabad is known for brassware, Khurja for pottery, Agra for marble inlay work in the tradition of the Taj Mahal, and Varanasi for wooden toys as well as its silk.

sections.heading: Hands-on workshops
list: Block-printing sessions in and around Jaipur.
Pottery and blue-pottery classes in Jaipur.
Short weaving and embroidery visits in Kutch villages, arranged through local organisations.

safety: Buy from government emporia, cooperatives, certified sellers or artisans directly; look for GI tags, Silk Mark or Handloom Mark where they apply, and be wary of 'factory visits' arranged by touts.
Get receipts for expensive items, and ask about shipping and export rules for antiques; objects over 100 years old cannot be exported.
packing: Bubble wrap or soft clothes for pottery

faqs.q: What are the famous handicrafts of India?
faqs.a: Blue pottery, block printing, Bidriware, dhokra, Pattachitra, Madhubani painting, Channapatna toys and Kashmiri papier-mache are among the best known.
A Geographical Indication that protects a product's name for goods made in a particular place, such as Channapatna toys.

faqs.q: Where can I see craftspeople at work?
faqs.a: In craft villages such as Raghurajpur and the villages around Bhuj, and at fairs like Surajkund.

faqs.q: Which is the best craft fair in India?
faqs.a: The Surajkund International Crafts Mela near Delhi is the best known.

faqs.q: Can I export antiques from India?
faqs.a: Objects over 100 years old are antiquities and cannot be exported without permission.
